title: Field operational runway and safety windows for private deployments
author: Asha Kumar
body:
Summary
-------
This document defines the operational "runway" (how much maintenance/upgrade activity a private deployment can safely absorb) and the safety window model used by Redwood field engineers and customer operators when performing upgrades, scheduled maintenance, or emergency changes in Private/VPC/on-prem deployments. It codifies threshold-based decision logic, a step-by-step maintenance procedure, required telemetry, and an explicit rollback decision matrix.

Scope
-----
- Applies to Redwood Private deployments (VPC and on-prem) that are in steady-state or candidate for minor/major upgrades.
- Focus areas: control plane updates, runtime (serving) upgrades, model swaps, KV cache migrations, host/firmware maintenance, network failover drills.
- Not in scope: initial provisioning, hardware replacement performed by vendor field engineering.

Goals and guarantees
--------------------
- Maintain customer-visible SLOs during maintenance where possible: 99.95% availability, p95 request latency < 250ms for small-sequence (<128 tokens) requests on Dedicated/VPC tiers.
- Define conservative safety windows that minimize customer impact and provide clear abort/rollback criteria.
- Provide deterministic, auditable decision points for executing and stopping changes.

Ownership and points of contact
------------------------------
- Runbook owner: eng-private-deployments / Field Ops (primary contact: Asha Kumar)
- Escalation: oncall-eng-sre -> eng-platform -> eng-serving-runtime
- Customer notifications: customer-success lead for the account and the assigned solutions engineer

Prerequisites (pre-change checklist)
-----------------------------------
1) Deployment health baseline (must be green):
   - all control-plane replicas Ready == true
   - model-router healthy_count >= 95%
   - KV cache hit rate within expected range for the last 24h (> 60% for workloads that pin caching)
   - no P1 incidents in last 72 hours
2) Telemetry and backups:
   - recent backup of kv-cache snapshot (if migrating) stored in customer-verified S3/GCS location
   - control-plane audit log collection enabled and accessible
3) Communication:
   - customer has agreed to maintenance window via ticket (include start/end times and rollback SLAs)
   - field operator sprints scheduled and oncall covered
4) Resources reserved:
   - additional capacity (burst nodes) reserved for at least the maintenance window + 1 hour
   - temp SLA override approved for <1 hour if needed

Runway model (how much change the system can absorb)
--------------------------------------------------
We use a three-tier runway model: Green, Amber, Red. Determine runway by evaluating the last 72-hour telemetry snapshot and current load forecast.

- Green (safe): CPU utilization < 60% cluster-wide, p95 latency headroom >= 40% (i.e., p95 < 150ms), error rate < 0.05%
  - Allowed actions: non-disruptive config changes, minor runtime patch, model quantization swap with canary
- Amber (caution): CPU utilization 60–80%, p95 latency headroom 20–40% (p95 150–200ms), error rate 0.05–0.2%
  - Allowed actions: canary-only changes, staged capacity add before further changes; require two-person approval
- Red (unsafe): CPU utilization > 80%, p95 latency headroom < 20% (p95 > 200ms), error rate > 0.2% or any active P1
  - Allowed actions: emergency-only (no elective changes). Initiate mitigation or rollback immediately.

Decision flow (high level)
-------------------------
1) Prepare: run pre-change checklist and capture baseline snapshot (metrics, topology, recent errors).
2) Classify runway: Green/Amber/Red based on telemetry rules.
3) Approve: if Green, single-operator with ticket; if Amber, two approvers (field lead + eng-platform); if Red, halt and remediate.
4) Execute: follow change steps below with defined safety windows and automated checks.
5) Validate: run post-change acceptance tests and keep system in observation mode for a defined time.
6) Commit or Rollback: if any automated check fails or threshold exceeded, trigger rollback immediately according to the rollback matrix.

Safety windows and canonical timeslices
--------------------------------------
- Safety window definition: a contiguous time slice following a change step during which the system is observed for regressions.
- Standard safety window durations (default):
  - Minor config or small runtime patch: 10 minutes per canary batch, 30 minutes stabilization after final rollout.
  - Model swap / quantization swap: 15 minutes per canary batch, 60 minutes stabilization after final rollout.
  - Control-plane rolling restart: 5 minutes per replica, 45 minutes stabilization after last replica.
  - KV cache migration or shard move: 30 minutes per shard, 120 minutes stabilization.

Automated checks during safety windows
-------------------------------------
- Must execute automated health checks at t=0, t=window/2, t=window end. Checks include:
  - service availability (100% for control-plane endpoints, >= 99.9% for runtime frontends during canary)
  - p95 latency not increasing by > 25% relative to baseline
  - 5xx error rate increase not exceeding 0.1 percentage points (absolute)
  - model output quality quick-check (see "Validation tests") not regressing by > 2% on selected prompt set
- If any check fails, trigger immediate stop and begin rollback.

Rollback decision matrix (quick reference)
-----------------------------------------
| Trigger | Severity | Action | Max time to rollback | Owner |
|---------|----------|--------|----------------------|-------|
| Control-plane replica failing to Ready for > 2x expected restart time | High | Pause rollout; if > 5 minutes, rollback | 10 minutes | field lead + eng-sre |
| p95 latency > baseline + 25% sustained for > 2 sampling intervals | Medium | Pause; increase capacity; if persists 15m, rollback | 15 minutes | eng-platform |
| 5xx rate increases > 0.5% absolute | High | Immediate rollback | 5 minutes | oncall-eng-sre |
| Model quality regression > configured threshold (default 2%) | High | Rollback model | 10 minutes | applied-ml + customer success |
| KV shard migration I/O errors > 0.1% | High | Abort migration and revert shard routing | 30 minutes | field ops |

Post-change validation tests (minimal set)
-----------------------------------------
1) Acceptance API smoke: 50 small (<=128 tokens) requests across 5 model families, verify 200 OK and response within p95 target.
2) Latency stability: collect p95 over 15 minutes and compare to baseline.
3) Model fidelity quick-check: run curated prompt-set (10 prompts) and compute BLEU-like similarity or application-specific metric.
4) Cost/throughput sanity: ensure token/sec throughput is within +/-10% of baseline for given capacity.

Telemetry and alerts required
---------------------------
- Metrics to be present and queried during maintenance:
  - control_plane_up_replicas, model_router_healthy, runtime_p95_latency_ms, runtime_5xx_rate, kv_cache_hit_rate, gpu_utilization_percent
- Alert thresholds (examples):
  - runtime_5xx_rate > 0.5% for 5m -> P1
  - runtime_p95_latency_ms > baseline * 1.25 for 10m -> P2
  - control_plane_up_replicas < expected -> P1

Telemetry example query (PromQL):
  - p95: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le))
  - control-plane ready: sum(up{job="control-plane"}) / expected_replicas

Change execution: step-by-step (example: model quantization swap)
---------------------------------------------------------------
1) Reserve runway and notify customer: open maintenance ticket and mark the deployment as "in-maintenance" in our deployment catalog.
2) Take a metadata snapshot: deployment-config.yaml and current model binary checksums.
3) Canary batch (5% of serving pods):
   - Push new quantized model to canary nodes with drain strategy disabled.
   - Run automated quick-checks at t=0 and t=7 minutes.
   - If checks pass, expand to 25% and repeat checks.
4) Full rollout in stages (25% -> 50% -> 100%), respecting the safety window durations above.
5) Post-rollout stabilization: run 60-minute fidelity and latency run.
6) Commit the change and close the maintenance ticket.

Emergency rollback playbook (when rollback decision is made)
-----------------------------------------------------------
1) Stop any ongoing rollout jobs and mark canaries as unhealthy to avoid traffic routing.
2) Initiate automated revert: redeploy previous model/artifact and, for runtime changes, restart in reversed order (last changed first).
3) If rollback fails to immediately restore health, escalate to eng-serving-runtime and prepare a hotfix trunk build.
4) Open a postmortem and notify customer with timeline and remediation plan.

Customer requirements mapping (how to interpret customer constraints)
-------------------------------------------------------------------
- Many customers require:
  - maintenance windows in their local business hours (e.g., 22:00–04:00 local)
  - advance notice: >= 72 hours for major changes, 24 hours for minor changes
  - evidence of backups and a signed rollback SLA for major schema or stateful changes
- Map customer contract clauses to runway: if contract requires zero-downtime, runway must be Green and a hot standby must be provisioned before any change.

Safe defaults (recommended settings)
----------------------------------
- Canary batch sizes: 5%, 25%, 50%, 100%
- Default model quality regression threshold: 2% on curated eval set
- Rollback hold window: immediately if any P1 or if >2 automated check failures in safety windows
- Reserve +20% burst capacity for any model-level change

Appendix A — CLI and API snippets
--------------------------------
- Take a baseline snapshot (example):
  $ redwood-deploy snapshot create --deployment-id=dp-1234 --label=pre-change-2026-03-01

- Start a staged rollout:
  $ redwood-deploy rollout start --deployment-id=dp-1234 --artifact=model-v2-quant --stages=5,25,50,100 --safety-window=15m

- Query canary health:
  $ rwsctl metrics query --expr 'runtime_5xx_rate{deployment="dp-1234"}[5m]'

Appendix B — Example stabilization matrix (text table)
-----------------------------------------------------
Trigger | Expected operator action | Time budget
-------|--------------------------|-----------
p95 latency increases by 10% in canary | Add burst capacity + monitor | 15 minutes
Any single 5xx in control-plane | Pause and investigate | 5 minutes
Model fidelity drop 1.5% | Continue at caution and expand slowly | 30 minutes

----------------------------

- See: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/upgrade-and-rollback/automated-sla-driven-canary-and-rollback-cookbook-2026 for automated rollback tooling and scripts

Notes and rationale
-------------------
This document intentionally favors conservative safety windows and early aborts to protect customer workload availability and to limit blast radius in private deployments where hardware heterogeneity and network constraints are common. The runway model reduces human uncertainty by converting telemetry into discrete operational states (Green/Amber/Red).
